subject: Bulbasaur
whyItWorks: Argues one clear thesis (the best-designed first Pokémon) instead of listing facts.
Evidence is concrete and checkable: Brock and Misty, Venusaur at level 32 versus Charizard and Blastoise at 36.
A real counterpoint (later Kanto punishes it) makes the verdict earned rather than fan service.
Authored information design: every scene has one headline claim plus 2-4 short labels that can become visuals.

episode.title: Why Bulbasaur Is the Perfect First Pokémon
episode.premise: Make Bulbasaur the hero and explain why #001 is such a strong first partner without turning the short into an infographic.
episode.audiencePromise: Show why early Kanto favors Bulbasaur, its starting dual type, fast evolution, and the later trade-offs that keep it balanced.
episode.openLoop: Why does Bulbasaur feel so perfectly designed as Pokémon #001?
episode.payoff: It gets an unusually friendly opening, starts as Grass/Poison, and reaches Venusaur early—but later matchups stop it from being a free win.

scenes.headline: WHY BULBASAUR WORKS SO WELL
scenes.narration: Bulbasaur might be the most perfectly designed first Pokémon.
scenes.caption: MEET NUMBER ONE

scenes.headline: BROCK. THEN MISTY.
scenes.narration: Right away, its Grass typing is great into Brock and Misty.
scenes.caption: A VERY FRIENDLY START

scenes.headline: GRASS + POISON
scenes.narration: And Bulbasaur is Grass and Poison from the very start.
scenes.caption: TWO TYPES. LEVEL FIVE.

scenes.headline: VENUSAUR AT LEVEL 32
scenes.narration: It reaches Venusaur at level thirty-two—four levels before Charizard or Blastoise.
scenes.caption: FULLY EVOLVED FIRST

scenes.eyebrow: BUT IT ISN'T A CHEAT CODE
scenes.headline: LATER KANTO PUSHES BACK
scenes.narration: Later, Fire, Psychic, Ice and Flying attacks can punish it hard.
scenes.caption: THE EASY START DOESN'T LAST

scenes.headline: WOULD YOU PICK BULBASAUR?
scenes.narration: So—if you started Kanto again today, would you pick Bulbasaur?
scenes.caption: #001. YOUR FIRST PICK?
